columns.name: Attributed origin of the SRL
columns.instruction: Copy, close to the source's own words, the prior work(s) the source credits for first establishing the square-root law (SRL) for covert communication, classical or quantum. Include author names or reference descriptions only as the source gives them. If the source presents itself as establishing the SRL, say so. If the source does not attribute the SRL to anyone, leave the cell empty as not found.

columns.name: Contribution type
columns.instruction: Mark what the source proves about the covert limit in its own setting. Choose 'Achievability only' if it gives only a coding scheme or lower bound. Choose 'Converse only' if it gives only an upper bound. Choose 'Both (capacity/tight scaling)' if it gives matching or both bounds. Choose 'Applies or extends a known SRL' if it uses an established SRL without proving new bounds. Choose 'Breaks or circumvents the SRL' if it shows more than O(√n) is possible.

options.label: Applies or extends a known SRL

columns.name: Channel model
columns.instruction: Mark the channel model or models the source analyses. If several are treated, mark all of them. Use 'Other' for a model not listed.

columns.name: Warden (detector) model
columns.instruction: Mark how the source models the warden's detection capability. Mark all that apply. 'Photon counting / direct detection' applies only if the source states that the warden counts photons or uses direct detection. 'Quantum-limited / arbitrary measurement' applies when the warden may use any quantum measurement. Choose 'Not specified' if the source does not describe the warden's receiver.

columns.name: Covert payload scaling
columns.instruction: Mark the scaling in n channel uses that the source states for the amount that can be sent covertly and reliably. If the source gives different scalings under different conditions, mark each one it states. Choose 'Not stated' if no scaling is given.

columns.name: What is transmitted
columns.instruction: Mark the kind of payload whose covert scaling the source analyses. Mark all that apply.

columns.name: Signal power / photon-number constraint
columns.instruction: Copy, close to the source's own words, how the source limits the transmitted signal so that it stays undetected. Examples are the mean photon number or energy per channel use scaling as 1/√n, or sparse signaling with about √n active uses. Include any stated dependence on the warden's noise or detector. If the source gives no such constraint, leave the cell empty as not found.

columns.name: Covertness metric
columns.instruction: Mark the measure the source uses to define undetectability. Mark all that are used. Choose 'Not stated' if the source does not name one.
